lines.tts: Some saadhus never cut their hair. Some shave it all off. Why?

caps: Because our old texts | describe *TWO ROADS* | out of the world.
lines.tts: Because our old texts describe two roads out of the world.

caps: *MANU* says | he must wear *JATA,* | beard and nails uncut.
lines.tts: Road one: the forest hermit. Manu says he must wear jataa, beard and nails uncut.

caps: So when *RAM* | left for the forest,
lines.tts: So when Raam left for the forest, he asked for banyan milk, and matted his own hair.

caps: He owns nothing. | His head is *SHAVEN.*
lines.tts: Road two: the wandering sannyaasi. He owns nothing. His head is shaven. Even the shikhaa is given up.

caps: One never cuts. | One cuts it all.
Both threw away | the same thing: | the *COMB.*
lines.tts: One never cuts. One cuts it all. Both threw away the same thing: the comb.

caps: Today, many who follow *SHIVA,* | the matted-haired,
lines.tts: Today, many who follow Shiva, the matted-haired, keep jataa, like the Naaga saadhus. Dandee sannyaasis, staff in hand, stay shaven.

caps: But even a *NAGA* | begins with a *SHAVED HEAD,*
lines.tts: But even a Naaga begins with a shaved head, on the day of his deekshaa.

caps: Matted or shaven, | if it's only for the stomach,
lines.tts: And Bhaja Govindam says: matted or shaven, if it's only for the stomach, it's just a costume.

caps: Where did *YOU* last see | a sadhu with *JATA?*
lines.tts: Where did you last see a saadhu with jataa? Comment the place!
